title: 2015 AMC 12B 12
statement: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) be three distinct one-digit numbers. What is the maximum value of the sum of the roots of the equation \((x - a)(x - b)\) \(+ (x - b)(x - c) = 0?\)

solutions.text:
Factoring gives \((x - b)\bigl(2x - (a + c)\bigr) = 0,\) so the roots are \(b\) and \(\dfrac{a + c}{2}.\) Their sum is \(b + \dfrac{a + c}{2}.\)

Using distinct digits, take \(b = 9\) and \(a + c = 8 + 7 = 15,\) giving \(9 + 7.5 = 16.5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The roots are \(b\) and \(\dfrac{a + c}{2};\) maximize \(b + \dfrac{a + c}{2}\) over distinct digits
